reviews.review: absolutely amazing story, great gameplay and a ton of fun if youre playing with friends

"Dark Souls with guns" is the perfect description.
The voice acting could be better; the humans are passable, but the other races carry the voice acting quite well.
The music is a delight and the art direction works amazingly well. Each world has a distinct feel to it and they work perfectly to tell a story.
The gameplay is satisfying, but some bosses will be a little frustrating depending on your build; thankfully, respeccing and changing up your archetypes allows for a lot of build variety.

Take your time with it, and don't be afraid to feel lost; the game doesn't ell you much but everything becomes apparent as you progress.

I... have no idea why I've decided that this game is worth either my time or my money. But I was wrong. Will, maybe, buy it again later for some, say, 10 USD just to try again with all the patches and simply for collection. But it's definitely not worth 20 USD in my region now. That's the price for some God of War, not this. Or a fresh RoboCop, with nice graphics, alright performance, and meaningful cutscenes.

What about the game itself, regardless of its price. On the Steam Deck (15W) rigth from the beginnig you'll be met with an FSR2 being set to performance (or ultra performance) where bluriness is so bad that you can see the second character running right after yours like a shadow (it's a blur, not an actual character). The same for the real second character being seen from far away -- it's not easily distinguishable from the environment. Okay, you'll switch to balance or quality and set a limit at 30 fps. I may not like the genre but it's a personal preference, alright. The navigation through the menu is being completely performed with your analog stick (not partially, and mixed with the dpad, like in Hogwarts Legacy) -- I have no idea why this is considered a "full gamepad supported" game, while its menus are typical grids and lines totally suitable for the dpad of any gamepad. Even if you're okay with that, the moment you reach the hub you see an fps being cut in half (so you'll probably have to return to performance or ultra performance? that's why I've described it in details previously). So overall, I can't recommend it, even for 20 USD. Sometime later for 10 USD, as an already old game, just for collection -- maybe.

I regret not asking for a refund sooner. *updated at bottom*

Veteran gamer here. started on easy/normal mode, tried for about 4.5 hours in and the game is just way too ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hard. Your character is slow, dodges don't roll far enough to get out of the way, it is way too easy to get stunlocked where you cant move fast enough to run. Dodges often aren't able to fire because you cant stand up. Enemies close distance so much faster than you can move, so you often end up in a situation where it is impossible to create space. On top of that there are often waves of easier creatures when you encounter a boss, that also do tons of dmg. Lastly, it is far too easy to run out of ammo.

Controls are funky and make it super easy to accidentally use the rare resources/healing by accident. After reworking the controls I have this happen less often, but why tf would the game let me use items for healing or clearing status when I am uninjured or don't have the status. Super easy to burn through resources.

Why is normal mode so damn impossible!! Would be fun if I could just play the story, but I can't even get through some of the early sections.

The 3rd person aiming is so incredibly clunky (pc with mouse and keyboard here, so it shouldn't be hard, but it is just awkward). no mission log, so if I missed something I don't actually know what I am supposed to be searching for. (update, there is not enough depth to need a mission log, so not a loss if you can say that). Not enough instructions on crafting to help you figure out how to min max without wasting hours. (update, you don't need to craft, really for any reason - you visit the armory to upgrade your weapons and that is about it. zzzzz)

Let's add on top of this, poor/annoying voice acting, and a fairly shallow story (started off interesting, but I haven't had anything to progress it in ages, very dull.)

Overall I really regret buying this, glad I got it on sale instead of wasting the full 50$.

Do not buy, and smash your head against the wall in frustration like I have been....

**Update** - After not being able to get a refund because I had spent more than 2 hrs playing, I thought I would try it for a while longer to see if it got any better. The first 5 or so hours was an absolute slog until finally gaining a few levels and some items that made my hero's damage output actually accomplish anything. This was *miserable* to get through. After that, progress happened a lot more quickly, but still never reached a place where the game felt tolerable. Level design (procedurally generated) is incredibly banal. Aesthetically the game gets super tiresome very fast. Enemies, once you have the items to fight them, quickly become stale. Bosses add a new element briefly, with 1 or 2 infuriating tries before you figure out the handful of combos they do, and then they just become a drag.

Lastly, you never feel like you get any character level progression, beyond the super painful first hurdle, as the enemies are always 1 level above you character, so you cant even go back to easier areas to feel progress, as this inst a thing. 

In 13 hours there has been ZERO story advancement, hell the story was barely even established in the first place. No reason for me to care about the characters, as there has not been any events to create any story, let alone anything to get me invested in the dragging game play. At least the voice acting for the 3 NPCs you encounter out in the world and the world 1 boss improved, but that is not enough of a redeeming factor.

The second world, "the labyrinth" is the dullest level design and makes me want to rip my eyes out it is SO GREY.

I thought once I got to where the game was actually playable that I would stick it out until I had put in 30 hrs or so, to get my play time to ~1$/hr, but I have reached a point where I am convinced this is the most abhorrent game play experience I have suffered through since COD Black Ops Cold War. (fundamentally different game, but also fundamentally bad). Except this game requires a substantially greater investment of time. And I just can't. I can't continue to suffer through this dull digital effluent of a game.

I was hesitant to buy this game at first.  Many reviewers said it was a very hard game - and it was for about the first 6 hours or so.  I am just a scrub playing when I can for fun!  Honesty, I'm not very good, however, I managed to beat this game on Survivor and got all the way to the final boss battle at the Blackened Citadel on Veteran playing solo (still stuck on that fight).  Having said all this, I absolutely love this game!  It is truly brilliant in its approach to customization of load outs and play style.  You must evaluate each encounter and make adjustments to Archetype, skills, armor, amulets and rings.  So many options!  Sometimes it takes many tries to figure something out that works, but there always is a way.  Also, you must learn the  mechanics of each boss encounter.  There is a lot of movement needed to dodge.  I found this difficult with a keyboard and mouse, so I switched to an Xbox One controller.  Game support for the controller is flawless.  This proved to be much easier for me to handle the movement intensive requirements.  To me, this game is a blend of Metro and Diablo with an overtone of the Matrix.  My one wish is that we get another completely new world to play around in, not just a new area of an existing world.  The first expansion is definitely worth the price.  The new Ritualist Archetype is one of my two favorites (also love the Invader).  Great  addition to the game.  Hope the support from Gunfire Games continues......I'll be playing this game for a long time due to the fun factor and replay value.  Working now on unlocking the Archon.  Still lots to do after 140 hours!

While I'm not a big fan of the overall story, each world has a story line that I adore. The combat is fun and can be surprisingly difficult despite you having guns instead of just a sword. There is plenty to strive for, plenty to use your power on, and plenty of people to use your power with. Overall a great game for both solo and coop players.

Satisfying gunplay, myriads of secrets, excellent replayability!

10/10
